Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1. Heard Sri Amit Kumar Srivastava, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Ashutosh Srivastava,
learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
2.

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: This is the second bail application on behalf of the applicant.

The first one was rejected by this
Court vide order dated 27.01.2023.

3. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No.188 of 2018, under Sections 498A, 304B I.P.C. and 3/4
D.P. Act, Police Station Shivali, District Kanpur Dehat, during the pendency of trial.

Arguments On Behalf Of Applicant:
Vikas vs State Of U.P. on 12 August, 2024

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81265040/
1

4.
As new ground, in all seven witnesses have been examined and the trial is moving at a snail's pace.
There is no likelihood of conclusion of trial in near future as only seven witnesses have been examined and several witnesses need to be examined further.
5. The fundamental rights of the applicant enshrined under Article 21 of the Constitution of India stand violated.
6. The cause of death has been found to be asphyxia as a result of ante-mortem hanging.
7. The criminal history assigned to the applicant stands explained in paragraph 21 of the affidavit filed in support of the bail application.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 02.06.2018.
He is ready to cooperate with trial.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF STATE BY A.G.A./INFORMANT:
8.
The bail application has been opposed but the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant could not be disputed.

CONCLUSION:
9. ?The Supreme Court in the case of Union of India vs. K.A. Najeeb, AIR 2021 SC 712, has observed as under:-
"We are conscious of the fact that the charges levelled against the respondent are grave and a serious threat to societal harmony.

entities.text: Union of India vs. K.A. Najeeb, AIR 2021 SC 712
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Had it been a case at the threshold,
we would have outrightly turned down the respondent's prayer.

However, keeping in mind the length of the period spent by him in custody and the unlikelihood of the trial being completed anytime soon, the High Court appears to have been left with no other option except to grant bail."
10.
The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.

11. ?A person's right to life and liberty, guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because the person is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt.

Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the procedure must be just and reasonable.

The said principle has been recapitulated by the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690.
12.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: ?Reiterating the aforesaid view the Supreme Court in the case of Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595 has again emphasised that the very well-settled principle of law that bail is not to be withheld as a punishment is not to be forgotten.

entities.text: Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is high time that the Courts Vikas vs State Of U.P. on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81265040/
2 should recognize the principle that "bail is a rule and jail is an exception".
13.

entities.text: Courts Vikas vs State Of U.P. on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: ?Learned A.G.A. could not bring forth any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.
14. ?It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned A.G.A.
15.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case,
the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

16. Let the applicant-Vikas involved in aforementioned case crime number be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
17. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.

18. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.

(Justice Krishan Pahal)
